name: Civil Air Patrol Cadet Program (California Wing)
org: Civil Air Patrol, California Wing (U.S. Air Force Auxiliary)
city: California (squadrons in eight regional groups, Los Angeles to San Diego)
what_you_do: Cadets join a local squadron for weekly meetings. They learn leadership, aerospace and fitness. They can take orientation flights and go to events and an encampment.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 12 to 18 (the page is titled 'Become a Cadet (Ages 12-18)'). The page says your local squadron can answer eligibility questions.
pay_detail: Dues plus uniforms. The cost page (2021 and 2022 figures) lists $45 national dues, $25 squadron dues (can be waived for hardship), and about $205 to $300 total to join with uniforms. Encampment was $300 in 2021, with financial help available. No 2026 figures are posted, so check the National site for current dues.
deadline_text: Join any time. Attend about three meetings, then complete the application.
how_to_apply: Find a local squadron. Contact it and visit with a parent. Go to about three meetings. Then apply. You can apply online if your squadron commander says you are eligible, or by mail or fax. Contact: pao@cawgcap.org.
notes: Prices on the California Wing cost page are from 2021 and 2022. Ask your squadron for current amounts. The Northern California Bay Area squadrons are listed on the wing site. The cost page says you must go to encampment to advance to Cadet Second Lieutenant.
